To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy reconstruction employed in the XENON10 and XENON100 experiments is based only on the primary photon signal, that the usual energy scale is a factor x2 smaller in the lower left of the typical search region, and that the usual energy resolution is x1.5 smaller in the lower right of the typical search area.

the nuclear recoil energy scale is smaller than expected in the lower left region of the search space, and that a more accurate representation for search results is obtained by including the electron signal in the energy reconstruction.

the energy reconstruction based on both scintillation and ionization signals yields a more realistic picture of the search results, and the XENON experiment is not yet sensitive to a WIMP-nucleon spin-independent cross-section of ~10-43 cm2 for mWIMP~10 GeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of new techniques for the analysis of data from direct dark matter searches.
the energy reconstruction of nuclear recoils in liquid xenon detectors and its impact on direct detection dark matter searches.
the energy scale of the XENON experiment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nuclear recoil calibration data are consistent with a nuclear recoil energy scale that is about 2 times larger than the one usually employed.
, for the XENON1T dark matter search, the expected sensitivity is improved by a factor of x2 in the region of interest.
the XENON10 and XENON100 experiments have not yet excluded the possibility that the WIMP-nucleon elastic scattering cross section is of the order of 1 pb.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy resolution of liquid xenon detectors is improved by about a factor 2 when the electron signal is used.
the usual energy scale for nuclear recoils is underestimated by a factor of 2.
the nuclear recoil energy scale should be adjusted for dark matter search experiments, to avoid a bias in the interpretation of results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when considering the sensitivity of liquid xenon dark-matter searches, it is necessary to take into account both the nuclear recoil energy and the nuclear recoil calibration.
the nuclear recoil energy reconstruction should be based on the combined scintillation and ionization signals.
the energy reconstruction method used for the analysis of data should be chosen carefully, as it has a significant effect on the results of the search.
